title: Douglas S
content: I was hit by a car while riding a motorcycle. A friend behind me witnessed the accident. I crashed headfirst through the windshield. I was thrown back about thirty feet, landing flat on my back. Fortunately, helmet laws were in effect at the time. I remember landing on the pavement and losing consciousness. I clearly recall looking down at myself, lying in the street from a height of about fifteen feet. I watched this happening without any sense of time; it just was. Suddenly, I was back in my body, like smoke sucked into a vacuum. I was overwhelmed by excruciating pain. My left leg had a compound fracture, and I just wanted to get up and go home. The paramedics put an air cast on my leg. When they inflated it, I lost consciousness again. I remember fading in and out of consciousness in the back of the ambulance. I was experiencing terrible pain, that I hadn’t felt until I returned to my body. I woke briefly in the emergency room, telling nobody in particular that, "It hurt so badly I wished I were dead." The next morning, I awoke in a hospital room, facing a minimum six-month recovery. What stands out most about my experience is hovering above myself like a spectator, completely free of pain.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes, Accident, Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I clearly left my body and existed outside it
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: Less consciousness and alertness than normal, It was as if I was in a light haze. I could see fine, just a haze was present. Like a cloudy day is the best way I can describe it.
elements.At what time during the experience were: While hovering over myself in the street.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: My vision was the same. I was viewing the accident as a spectator from above.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: I don't recall any sound until I returned to my body.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: It was as though that wasn't me lying in the street.
elements.What was your religion prior to your exp: Christian- Protestant, I was just a child. I felt there was a God, but I didn't dwell on it much.
elements.Have your religious practices changed si: Yes, I believe completely that I was about to die until God intervened.
elements.What is your religion now?: Other or several faiths, I am spiritual. God is everywhere. I don't have to meet him in a brick-and-mortar structure.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I was a child just living life. I was totally confused by the experience. I thought maybe it wasn't real, but the memories I have are so vivid and have not faded through the years.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, Life became more valued, and I realized a life can be snuffed out in the blink of an eye.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: I wanted to be a better person given this new opportunity.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, I was absolutely clueless as to whether it was real. I never said anything until I read my first NDE.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, It was a new experience for me. It was so strange and vivid.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: It was and is the strangest experience I have had in seventy-one years on this earth.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, My other memories were jumbled, but the hovering was so clear in my memory.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, I view it as I was about to die and God had other plans for me.
elements.Is there anything else that you would li: No, I have told my story as best I can.
elements.Did the questions asked and information: Yes, Why lie or exaggerate? That is my thinking. I would love to know more about what happened to me.
